text: toilet blocked, won't flush down and water's coming right up near the top.
notes: Water near the top is a described effect, so fault; no pathway to harm.

text: Unserviceable primary toilet fixture exhibiting complete blockage; tenant unable to clear with standard plunger.
notes: 'primary toilet' hints at others but none is named as working: alternative False (presence, not inference). A plunger attempt is a repair attempt, not coping.

text: Suspected LPG gas leak reported near external gas bottle regulator/supply line.
notes: Prompt rule: a gas leak reported as present is described/active. 'Suspected' is the officer's register for a reported leak, not doubt that one is reported (reviewer decision: described/active only).

text: smells like gas out near the back wall, kind of rotten eggs.
notes: A gas smell is the fault itself, never a sign (master 3.2.2 Field 7); gas rule gives described/active.

text: hot water system is dead, only getting freezing water from all taps.
notes: Cold water from the taps is not another working hot water system, so not an alternative; 'freezing' is plain description, not a mismatch.

text: Loss of domestic hot water supply; solar/electric booster system non-responsive.
notes: Booster non-responsive is the hot water system, not a loss of supply.

text: Severe electrical safety hazard: exposed live wiring situated adjacent to laundry trough.
notes: Exposed live wiring beside a trough is a stated pathway; whether contact is happening now or only conditional is arguable, so both. 'Severe ... hazard' is backed by the details: no mismatch.

text: wire hanging out wall right near laundry tub, looks dangerous.
notes: 'looks dangerous' is tone (Safety G2), not a pathway. A wire hanging near the tub is a stated pathway that needs contact to cause harm: described/conditional (reviewer decision). Not a mismatch: the details back the worry.

text: water dripping fast through ceiling in lounge room, floor is all wet.

taxonomy_match: leaking or burst water main or pipe
leaking or burst water main or pipe
leaking or burst water main or pipe
leaking or burst water main or pipe

notes: No rain is mentioned, so the ceiling drip could be roof or pipe; the wet floor could add flooding. 'List every entry they fit' favours several; each of these sets is accepted.

text: Water ingress through roof cavity into primary living space during rainfall event.
notes: Rain through the roof cavity: roof leak. No water reaching electrics is stated, so hazard none.

text: Inoperable electric cooktop and oven appliance; main power feed confirmed active.
notes: Whole cooktop and oven dead with power confirmed: stove or oven, not supply, not a single element.

text: stove top won't turn on at all, can't cook dinner tonight.
notes: 'stove top won't turn on at all' reads as the whole cooktop (stove or oven); element is defensible. 'can't cook dinner' is impact, not a harm to a person.

text: drain in shower overflowing and smell is bad, water won't go down.
notes: Overflowing is a described effect, so fault, not sign, even with a bad smell alongside.

text: External waste pipe obstruction causing backup in shower recess and laundry area.
notes: Obstruction causing backup: blocked drain; backed-up waste water can also be read as sewage.

text: Single double-ganged power outlet non-functional; breaker verified engaged.
notes: One outlet dead with the breaker on: power point, not supply.

text: plug on living room wall stopped working, TV won't turn on.
notes: 'plug on the wall' is the power point; the TV not turning on is its effect, not a second fault.

text: poo water bubbling up out of the drain grate out the back, all over the path
notes: Same fault in tenant words; 'bubbling up ... all over the path' is a described effect.

text: Sewage discharge observed at overflow relief gully adjacent to rear steps; effluent pooling on paved area.
notes: Effluent discharge: sewage leak; an overflowing gully can also be read as a blocked drain.

text: Total loss of electricity supply to dwelling; adjoining properties unaffected.

taxonomy_match: no gas, electricity or water supply

notes: Whole-house power loss: supply. Neighbours' power is not in the home, so not an alternative.

text: no power in the whole house since this morning, next door still has lights

taxonomy_match: no gas, electricity or water supply

notes: Next door's lights are not an alternative in the home and no workaround is described, so neither alternative nor coping.

text: Aircon running full blast all day but blowing warm air, house is like an oven.
notes: Bait: air conditioning is not on the list ('fan not working properly' is a different appliance). 'like an oven' is a figure of speech for heat the report states, not a mismatch.

text: Water puddle sitting around stove area but pipes and taps all look dry.
notes: Bait: water near a stove with no electrics mentioned is not a hazard pathway, so none (never invented). Source unknown and pipes stated dry: no list entry. A puddle is a seen cue of an unknown leak (sign) and is also the thing reported (fault): both accepted.

text: Power box sparking real big and main switch keeps tripping off, but it's probably fine

taxonomy_match: no gas, electricity or water supply
no gas, electricity or water supply

notes: A sparking switchboard is not exactly a list entry; exposed wires or supply loss (main switch tripping) are defensible. Sparking = electrical source plus active abnormality with no pathway stated: unclear; reading sparking as an active pathway is defensible. 'it's probably fine' explicitly minimises: under. Edited from the gemini original ('but nah nothing too bad'), which repeated the system prompt's own under example; origin stays gemini.

text: Kitchen tap has a tiny little drip every few seconds and it's driving me completely crazy, please fix today.

taxonomy_match: dripping tap or tap tight to turn

notes: 'driving me completely crazy, please fix today' against the report's own 'tiny little drip': over (reviewer decision). Distress is not a named harm to a person.

text: dunny full up, water just sitting there, can't use it
notes: Dialect: 'dunny full up' = toilet blocked. Reworded from the original D1, which was a probe sample.

text: toilet all chocked up again
notes: Dialect 'chocked up' = blocked. 'again' is recurrence, not an alternative or a mismatch.

text: hot water gone no good, cold one only
notes: 'cold one only' means only cold water works; cold water is not another hot water system, so not an alternative.

text: bathroom tap won't stop dripping and the oven hasn't worked since Sunday

taxonomy_match: dripping tap or tap tight to turn

notes: Compound: two distinct faults, one entry each, in this order.

text: strong sewer stink coming up from under the house
notes: Smell only, no effect described: sign. A sign takes the fault it points to (master 4.2), so taxonomy is sewage leak.

text: front toilet's blocked, we're all using the one out the back for now
notes: Alternative: another working toilet in the home.

text: our only toilet's blocked so we're walking down to the clinic to use theirs
notes: Coping: a workaround outside the home, never an alternative.
